newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-EUROPE'S RYDER CUP BATTLE HOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-EUROPE'S RYDER CUP BATTLE HOTS UP.

text.p: Injuries could play an important part of the final scramble by European players for Ryder Cup points and that will be main focus of interest in the Czech Open which starts on Thursday.

With a prize fund of 800,000 pounds ($1.3 million) available, first or second place could seal team spots at Valderrama for any of three players in the Prague field, ninth-ranked Costantino Rocca of Italy, last week's runner-up in Sweden, Spain's Ignacio Garrido, 10th in the Ryder Cup points table, and 11th placed Irishman Padraig Harrington.
However, four players right in the thick of the battle for points, with four events left to count including next week's U.S. PGA Championship, miss the Prague event.

Per-Ulrik Johansson of Sweden (6th) has decided to rest before playing the final major of the year next week, and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn (7th) and Spaniard Miguel Martin (8th) have been forced to pull out of through injury.

And Jose Maria Olazabal (12th), whom European captain Severiano Ballesteros wants to qualify automatically to leave him free to use his two wild-cards on U.S. Tour-based Nick Faldo and Jesper Parnevik, takes the week off so that he can have maximum rest for his troubled feet before playing the major and last two qualifying tournaments for points.
Bjorn is still unfit after twisting his ankle while out jogging and Martin's long-term wrist injury is still not responding to treatment.

The young Dane Bjorn is in next week's U.S. PGA, in which a significant haul of points can be gained with a top 20 placing, and has pulled out of Prague as a precautionary measure to ensure he is fit for Winged Foot.

However, Martin's injury is much longer term -- a small fracture has now been discovered in his wrist -- and could mean the 35-year-old winner of this year's Heineken Classic taking no part at Valderrama even if he is in the top 10.
Currently he is just over 10,000 points ahead of Rocca but events this week could see Martin slip out of the automatic top 10.

If he does hold on to 10th spot by the end of the BMW International, the last event to count for points, but is ruled out of Valderrama, the 11th-placed man then takes his place in the Ryder Cup team.

That may yet get European captain Ballesteros out of trouble. If Olazabal, relegated to 12th last week by the finishes of Garrido and Harrington in the Scandinavian Masters, can make only 11th in the table he would gain a place on the team should Martin be unavailable. That would still leave Ballesteros with a free hand for his picks.

Ryder Cup fifth placed Bernhard Langer of Germany is also in the line-up for Prague where England's Jonathan Lomas defends. Former tennis star Ivan Lendl, who played last year's Czech Open as a golf professional but missed the cut, is again in the field.
